ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Frances Burney — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Review three weeks after right mastectomy; start of endocrine therapy and survivorship care

text.paragraph: Review three weeks after right mastectomy. [S]

Mrs. Burney returns three weeks after a right total mastectomy with sentinel node biopsy. The breast MRI before surgery showed a second 0.8 cm cancer at 7 o'clock, confirmed by MRI-guided biopsy, so with Dr. Marsh she chose mastectomy; she did not want reconstruction. The germline panel showed no pathogenic variant. She had general anesthesia with a pectoral nerve block, was told of each step beforehand, and went home the next morning. Her pain was 2 out of 10 by the third day; she needed no opioid at home and stopped acetaminophen at two weeks. A seroma after drain removal was aspirated once by the surgical team eleven days ago and has not returned. The pathology shows multicentric invasive ductal carcinoma, 2.6 cm and 0.8 cm, grade 2, with clear margins and 0 of 3 sentinel nodes involved. The recurrence score is 13. Dr. Marsh and the breast program's medical oncologist advise five years of anastrozole, with no chemotherapy and no radiation. She has a little numbness under the right arm and is doing her shoulder exercises. Her bone density scan this morning shows low bone mass. [S]

list.item:
Multicentric right breast cancer, pT2(m) pN0(sn), hormone receptor positive, HER2 negative, after total mastectomy (C50.411). Curative surgery with clear margins and negative nodes. A recurrence score of 13 in a postmenopausal woman with node-negative disease means chemotherapy would add no benefit, and radiation is not needed after mastectomy for this stage. [S]
Anastrozole 1 mg daily from today for five years.
Written survivorship care plan given today: treatment summary, surveillance schedule, side effects of anastrozole, and whom to call.
History and examination every three to six months; diagnostic mammogram of the left breast in August, one year after diagnosis; no routine blood tests or body imaging.

Low bone mass on baseline DXA, with vitamin D insufficiency (M85.80). Lumbar spine T-score -1.4 and femoral neck -1.7, with a 10-year major fracture risk of about 8 percent; anastrozole speeds bone loss. Treatment with a bone medicine is not indicated at this risk. Vitamin D 24 ng/mL. [S]
Vitamin D3 1000 units daily and about 1200 mg of calcium a day, mostly from food.
Weight-bearing and strength exercise.
Repeat DXA in two years, sooner if a fracture occurs.

Anastrozole, starting today (Z79.811). Baseline: no joint pain, hot flashes, or vaginal dryness. LDL cholesterol 132 mg/dL, to be followed on an aromatase inhibitor. [S]
Report joint pain, hot flashes, or vaginal dryness; exercise helps joint aches.
Lipids yearly on anastrozole.
